$$2 \uparrow^{k+1} 2 \;=\; 2 \uparrow^k(2) \;=\; 4 \quad\text{by the induction hypothesis.} \qquad\blacksquare$$

**Corollary.** The right-hand side satisfies $2 \uparrow^{n+2} 2 = 4$ for all $n$ with $n+2 \ge 1$, i.e., for all $n \ge -1$.
